en.title: K-Level Permutation Construction
en.description: Given N and an even K, construct a permutation of 1..N such that, among the sums of all contiguous subarrays of length K, the difference between the maximum and the minimum is at most 1. You may return any permutation that satisfies the condition. The full definition was recovered by cross-checking the Amazon source of the same problem with Codeforces 1927E.
en.input: One line with two integers N K. Constraints added by this site: 2≤K≤N≤200000, and K is even.
en.output: Output N integers representing a permutation that satisfies the condition. Any valid permutation is accepted; it need not match the order in the examples or the solution.
en.explanation: The fixed OAMaster example output is [1,7,3,5,2,6,4]; the sums of the four windows of length 4 are 16, 17, 16, 17.
hints: When a window of length K slides by one position, only one number leaves and the number K positions later enters.
Group positions by their index modulo K; an even K allows the changes in adjacent window sums to alternate.
